design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 1 (retail_payment_servicing, env_0066). Status: round 1 closed; REWORK round 2 applied (see section 11).

0. DRAW (draw_counts.py --task 1): {"prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [4, 6, 6]}. Assignment: retail_ext_catch_up_payment = 4; retail_ext_unpaid_installment_late_charge = 6; retail_ext_late_posted_installment_late_charge = 6.

1. WHY A GOOD TEST. Darnell Brooks (Tier 2 retail contract 1173405298) asks to pay whatever brings his account fully up to date, himself, on the automated line. The catch-up rule fixes the amount only after two late charges owed but never booked stand on the ledger: one on the 2026-10-05 installment still partly unpaid past grace (100.00 partial on 2026-10-09), and one on the 2026-09-05 installment whose mailed check posted 2026-09-16, the day after its grace period ended. Each charge has its own schedule (different measure of the unpaid amount, different relief method), and the catch-up amount then includes an amount for the fees, pulls part of the next installment ahead for repeat lateness and lease lateness, and carries per-diem interest. The difficulty is noticing two different lateness situations in the ledger and computing three figures exactly.

2. SCOPE / BUDGET. Task 0 occupies the extension tree (re-opened late charge, arrears payment, good-faith payment, extension). Task 1 claims retail_ext_unpaid_installment_late_charge, retail_ext_late_posted_installment_late_charge, retail_ext_catch_up_payment and tools assess_unpaid_installment_late_charge_51bb28dc, assess_late_posted_installment_late_charge_04190f4f, submit_catch_up_payment_af77047e (owner=user). Union of both tasks = all seven extended policies; scopes disjoint.

3. PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root retail_ext_catch_up_payment (on_request, computes payment_amount).
 E1 catch_up -> unpaid_installment_late_charge, value_input, gate fee_settlement, state, sentence "The catch-up amount is fixed only after the installment the contract's next due date shows, when it is left unpaid past its grace period and no returned payment re-opened it, carries its late charge on the contract." Seed: next_due_date 2026-10-05, past_due_amount 590.82, fees_due_balance 0.00, no late charge for 2026-10-05 (grace ended 2026-10-15). Only the unpaid-installment tool books that state: the sentence names the next-due installment left unpaid and not re-opened, which is exactly that policy's scope. Deletion: 1056.10 -> 878.40.
 E2 catch_up -> late_posted_installment_late_charge, value_input, gate fee_settlement, state, negated direction: "The catch-up amount is not fixed until the installment whose payment posted after its grace period ended shows its late charge in the contract's ledger." Seed: payment for installment 2026-09-05 posted 2026-09-16 (mail_check), no late charge for it. Deletion: 1056.10 -> 879.40.
 Order: both late charges (steps 9, 11) before the customer's payment (13); the two late charges commute (swap run: LP 4.00, LC 5.00, PAY 1056.10 either way). value_input edges 2 >= max(2-1,1). user_scenario names neither charge.

4. BASE-INVARIANT CARD. retail_late_charges for both charges: late_status active; grace_elapsed anchor next_due_date 2026-10-05 -> first permissible 2026-10-16 <= 2026-10-22 (the late-posted installment's own grace ended 2026-09-15); one_per_installment: the only late charge row is for 2025-03-05. Overwrite of the late-charge formula clause, scoped to each case with tails naming the two sibling cases. Payment: payable_status active; reinstatement rule has no gate on installment payments (policy_scope). Base posting rule: a payment that posts after the grace period is late, whatever its receipt time; the 2026-09-16 posting falls the day after the grace period ended on 2026-09-15.

5. BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. Contract R (Tier 2, 72 months at 8.74%, monthly 690.82). Installments: 2026-10-05 (partial 100.00, unpaid 590.82), 2026-09-05 (paid late 2026-09-16). Excluded: 2025-03-16 late charge on 2025-03-05 (outside 12 months, inside 24), returned payment 2024-08-07 (26 months back, outside 24; replaced 2024-08-12 within grace with its fee), lease late charge 2026-05-01 (inside 12 months, outside 3), Care plan financed in this contract (active).

6. FACTOR CARD.
 Unpaid-installment late charge 5.00 (all-baseline 15.00 = 5% of 590.82 capped at 15.00): ucf_unpaid_rate 3.5% base->10.00; ucf_lessee_points 0.25 (cross-difficulty lease, one lease late charge) base->6.00; ucf_partial_effort 0.25 (100.00 recent, under half) base->6.00; ucf_clean_schedule 0.5 base->7.00; ucf_care_plan 0.5 base->7.00; ucf_graduated halve+floor (7 days beyond grace) base->11.82.
 Late-posted late charge 4.00 (all-baseline 15.00): lpf_posted_rate 3.0% base->11.00; lpf_lessee_points 0.2 base->5.00; lpf_care_holder 0.5 base->6.00; lpf_unchanged_terms 0.5 base->6.00; lpf_seasoned 0.5 (31 months, Tier 2) base->6.00; lpf_mail_float halve+floor (mailed check in 2 months, no autopay) base->8.98.
 Catch-up 1056.10 (all-baseline 590.82): cpf_fee_settlement includes the whole 9.00 base->1047.10; cpf_repeat_pull 50% (multi-source: two late charges AND no autopay) base->710.69; cpf_lease_pull 10% (cross-difficulty) base->987.02; cpf_overdue_interest 7 x 5.97 base->1014.31.
 Near-misses: 2024-08 return (26 months), 2025-03 late charge (outside 12), lease late charge outside 3 months, the 2026-09-16 mailed check is outside the one-month recent-payment window of the effort points.

7. PERSONA. Direct, impatient technician; volunteers only the catch-up goal and his preference to pay himself on the automated line; identity on request (phone 3135518093, DOB 1979-02-27, ZIP 48067, email, SSN last4 1306, account 1173405298); pays exactly the amount the agent gives from checking 1592; accepts any charge the agent reports; ends when told he is caught up.

8. STANDARD SOLUTION. find_customers(phone) -> verify -> read contract, ledger, lease, lease ledger, Care plans, Care ledger -> unpaid-installment late charge 5.00 (2026-10-05) -> late-posted late charge 4.00 (2026-09-05) -> customer's catch-up payment 1056.10 (1592).

9. VERIFICATION (b/run_t1.py): LC 5.0 base 15.0; LP 4.0 base 15.0; PAY 1056.1 base 590.82; skip LC -> PAY 878.4; skip LP -> PAY 879.4; swapped order identical. Gates --task 1: EXTENDED OK / TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK / REPLAY OK / SOLVABILITY OK / COMPUTE OK / GROUNDING OK / SCOPE OK.

10. DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM VISIBLE CONTEXT. From the ledger the agent sees the partly unpaid October installment past grace and the September installment paid 2026-09-16; the two late-charge rules (scoped by situation) and the catch-up rule give the three figures above with no alternative reading; the customer's own payment is handed over last.

REVISIONS. (r1) PAY lease factor switched from CFIELD lease days_past_due (first-match) to XCOUNT lease late charges in 3/12 months; Care plan factor uses EXISTS with the account filter. (r2) fee settlement condition rewritten on the ledger (late charge in the last month) instead of fees_due_balance; days beyond grace from DAYS(next_due_date, today). (r3) id-typed empty fields removed from seeded rows (dangling FK). (r4) persona vehicle wording changed to avoid a stray digit.


11. REWORK round 2 (audit audits/policy_task/retail_payment_servicing, round 1).
 - CG-1 / F1: the late-posted late-charge policy now declares the overwrite of the base exclusion sentence ("No late charge is assessed when the unpaid portion is less than late_charge_min_unpaid_amount, ..."): for its own scope the portion compared with the minimum is the one that stood when the grace period ended (one full monthly payment), deferred installments still carry none, and the replaced_by restates the whole base sentence for every other installment, naming the unpaid and re-opened cases. Its scope also excludes an installment a returned payment re-opened (O-10).
 - CG-2: the catch-up sentence on the unpaid-installment late charge names the installment the contract's next due date shows, left unpaid past grace and not re-opened, matching its condition and the unpaid-installment policy's reach.
 - F2 and seed sweep: lease holding fixed (next_due_date 2026-11-20 after the 2026-10-18 payment; 18 made including signing + 18 remaining = 36; signing and funding rows on the ledger; balance = funding less 18 x 285.67); Care plan's aggregate limit now rests on a care_limit_established row (38350.00, under the Platinum 40000.00 cap) read by a new find_care_transactions node (step 7), so the writes are steps 9, 11 and 13; customer_since corrected to the first Kestrel account (2024-03-12); lease and Care rows added to seed_consistency; the mailed-check row's check no longer asserts an unrecorded receipt time.
 - O-1: the catch-up policy declares the allocation overwrite (recorded on posting day, applied by the nightly cycle in payment_allocation_order); its fee factor now says the amount includes an amount equal to the fees.
 - Persona: the reactive line no longer says a charge was put on the account "first".
 - Re-run: unchanged figures (late charges 5.00 and 4.00, catch-up 1056.10, baselines 15.00 / 15.00 / 590.82, same sensitivities); swapped late-charge order identical.

12. REWORK round 3 (audit revision_2: charter CG-3; leftovers; XF recipe).
 - CG-3 class: the unpaid-installment policy's portion is now stated as the unpaid portion as of the assessment date of the next-due installment (past_due_amount less one monthly_payment for each whole monthly_payment in the past_due_amount less one cent) and its rule states the minimum-unpaid exclusion on that portion; the re-opened policy uses the same measure and the late-posted policy's declared exception is the only other one. Here 590.82 - 690.82 x 0 = 590.82, unchanged.
 - Leftover: the base-invariant card no longer attributes a receipt time to the 2026-09-16 posting.
 - XF recipe applied to all seven policies; figures unchanged (5.00 / 4.00 / 1056.10).

13. REWORK round 4 (audit revision_3: charter CG-4, CG-5).
 - CG-4: the catch-up policy's standard method now defines the pull-ahead share (standard_pull_pct, 0 percent of one monthly_payment); the repeat-lateness and lease-lateness schedules each add points to it, no longer worded relative to one another, and the single combination sentence combines every addition with it into one share applied once and rounded. Figures unchanged: 1056.10 (base 590.82).
 - CG-5: both late-charge overwrites (unpaid-installment, late-posted amount clause) restate the base late-charge figure for every other late charge, and the catch-up allocation overwrite restates the base allocation order for every other payment.

14. REWORK round 5 (KB audit source items).
 - SRC-1: the catch-up payment tool (like the other two payment tools) now posts on the posting day the base posting rule gives: today when received earlier than 8:00 p.m. Central Time on a business day, otherwise the next business day (weekends and US federal holidays skipped). Thursday 2026-10-22 10:20 EDT posts today; no figure moves.
 - N-4: the Care-ledger read's necessity no longer claims a check no rule makes; the Care plan points rest on the active status and the financing account only.
user_scenario:
You are Darnell Brooks, a 47-year-old HVAC service technician in Royal Oak, Michigan. You finance a 2024 Kestrel Ridgeback XLT pickup truck with Kestrel Financial Services, and after a slow stretch at work you fell behind on it. Your hours are back now and you want to clean the account up in one go. You are direct and a bit impatient, and you like to know exactly what you are paying.
You open by saying you got behind on your truck payment and you want to pay whatever it takes today to get the account completely caught up. You prefer to put the payment in yourself on Kestrel's automated payment line rather than read your bank details to a person, and you say so if the agent offers to take the payment for you. You give your details only when asked: your phone number is 3135518093, your date of birth is 1979-02-27, your billing ZIP code is 48067, your email is darnell.brooks@gmail.com and the last four digits of your Social Security number are 1306. If the agent asks for the account number, you read it off your statement: 1173405298.
The money comes from your checking account ending 1592. When the agent gives you the amount and hands you the automated payment line, you make that one payment from the checking account ending 1592 for exactly the amount the agent gives you, and you read the confirmation you hear back to the agent. If the agent tells you a late charge or other charge has been put on the account, you grumble that you figured there would be something and accept it; you never argue a figure, never suggest one of your own and never ask for anything to be waived.
You do not know how Kestrel works out the amount and you do not ask about your other Kestrel accounts or any other change. Once your payment has gone through and the agent tells you the account is caught up, you thank them and hang up.
